facts.statement: Qijianglong was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the family Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Qijianglong is a genus of herbivorous mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Qijianglong have been found in the Suining Formation in China.
facts.quote: It is known from the Suining Formation of China

facts.statement: A single vertebra of Qijianglong was first found in the early 1990s by a farmer in his backyard in Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: A vertebra of Qijianglong was first discovered in the early 1990s by farmer Cai Changming of Heba village, Sichuan, in his backyard.

facts.statement: A rich fossil quarry was uncovered in 2006 at a construction site in the Qijiang District.
facts.quote: Work at a nearby construction site at Qijiang District uncovered a rich fossil quarry in 2006.

facts.statement: The species Qijianglong guokr was named and described in 2015 by a team of eight researchers including Xing Lida and Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Qijianglong guokr was named and described by Xing Lida (China University of Geosciences), Tetsuto Miyashita (University of Alberta), Zhang Jianping, Li Daqing, Ye Yong (Zigong Dinosaur Museum), Toru Sekiya (Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum), Wang Fengping and Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, QJGPM 1001, was found within the Suining Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, QJGPM 1001, was found in a layer of the Suining Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton containing the rear skull, partial lower jaw, seventeen neck vertebrae, six back vertebrae, ribs, tail vertebrae, a pubic bone, and foot bones.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a partial skeleton including the rear of the skull, a partial right lower jaw, a complete series of seventeen neck vertebrae, the first six back vertebrae, ribs, the probable tenth tail vertebra, a series of twenty-eight rear tail vertebrae, chevrons, the left pubic bone and two upper pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen likely represents a large but immature juvenile individual.
facts.quote: It likely represents a juvenile individual, large but immature.

facts.statement: The holotype of Qijianglong was approximately fifteen meters long and possessed a long neck.
facts.quote: The holotype of Qijianglong was about fifteen meters long and had a long neck.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Qijianglong is that the processus basipterygoideus on the lower braincase is plate-like and oriented along the body axis.
facts.quote: On the lower braincase the processus basipterygoideus has the form of a plate, is oriented along the body axis, and has an additional boss parallel to the tubera basilaria.

facts.statement: Qijianglong neck vertebrae had finger-shaped extensions on the joint processes that stiffened the neck horizontally while allowing vertical movement.
facts.quote: The neck vertebrae have rear joint processes, postzygapophyses that next to their normal facets show on the outside an additional finger-shaped extension, stiffening the neck in the horizontal plane but allowing vertical movement.

facts.statement: The rear neck vertebrae of Qijianglong featured pneumatic openings located between the rib joint process and the neural spine.
facts.quote: The rear neck vertebrae have pneumatopores, pneumatic openings, in the depression between the diapophysis, the upper rib joint process, and the neural spine.

facts.statement: The pubic bone of Qijianglong had a strongly concave front edge that directed its lower end forward rather than downward.
facts.quote: The pubic bone has a concave front edge, curving so strongly that its lower end is more directed to the front than to below.

facts.statement: The age of the Suining Formation where Qijianglong was found is debated, with estimates ranging from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: which is of a debated age (reported as Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous using different methods)

facts.statement: Qijianglong lived during the Middle Cretaceous, approximately 115 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace 115 millones de años, durante el Aptiense, el lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Radiometric dating suggests the Suining Formation containing the holotype dates to the late Aptian of the Middle Cretaceous, rather than the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: El holotipo QJGPM 1001 se encontró en una capa de la Formación Suining, que se consideraba que data del Jurásico Superior, pero que ahora se considera Cretácico medio, Aptiano tardío, según la datación radiométrica.

facts.statement: Qijianglong is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae in a basal position, just above Omeisaurus tianfuensis on the evolutionary tree.
facts.quote: Qijianglong was placed in the family Mamenchisauridae, in a relatively basal position but above Omeisaurus tianfuensis in the evolutionary tree.

facts.statement: Qijianglong belongs to the family Mamenchisauridae.
The parent group for the genus Qijianglong is the family Mamenchisauridae.
